---
name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit after each independently useful, verified proof/file/tooling
  change, before a long build or delegated review, and before expanding scope.
  A multi-hour implementation session should normally have several commits; one
  commit is appropriate only when the work is genuinely atomic. The message +
  diff is how progress is read, so use a semantic, math-first subject. Provenance
  trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Do not wait for the whole task to be complete. A checkpoint commit must build
  or otherwise be internally coherent, but it may explicitly leave the next
  named obligation open.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.CoverageDrop
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ThetaDegree

/-!
# The translated rank-one cover brick

This file records the part of the separably-closed cover argument that is already consumable by
the landed fibre API.  A `BaseFieldTranslationDrop` keeps the input class `lambda` in the
presentation equation, chooses its base-field translating class explicitly, and records the
positive-twist/point-subtraction output.  The consumer below turns that output into the exact
`IsSplitWitness` shape used by `chartLocus`.

The arbitrary-affine family of `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` objects required by
`PicRankOneOpen` is deliberately not inferred from `h0 = 1` and `H1 = 0`: no such producer is
landed in the current API.  The final theorem therefore exposes the field-level consumer and
keeps that family producer as an explicit integration obligation.
-/

set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
open TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The positive-twist input -/

section PositiveTwist

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]

/-- The FLV class theorem in the spelling used by the translated-cover lane.

The class `l` is the presenting class of the input fibre, while `theta` is the positive
base-field twist.  Keeping this as a named wrapper makes the positive-twist step visible at the
call site; it does not manufacture a presentation or hide the input class in an unrelated
existential. -/
theorem exists_positive_twist_vanishing
    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
    (l θ : Y.CechPic) (hθ : 1 ≤ classDeg K θ) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, ∀ W : Y.CurveDivisor,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K W = l * θ ^ n →
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1) := by
  exact exists_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_one_le_classDeg_of_isFinite_toP1
    π hπ l θ hθ

end PositiveTwist

/-!

The greedy translated-drop package records `h⁰ = 1` for `W₀ - S`, but it does not
assert that this chosen divisor is effective.  A positive global section nevertheless
produces an effective representative of the same class.  This file exposes that
representative with its degree-genus certificate, while retaining the input class and
the existing translated `IsSplitWitness` consumer.

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

section ResidualRepresentative

variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
  [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
  [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]

/-! The product curve instances are the same base-change package used by the
general producer.  `exists_effective_of_h0_pos` does not require the finite
cohomology instances, so this bridge only installs the geometric hypotheses. -/

theorem exists_effective_residual_degree_genus
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ)
    (r : SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (C := C) (L := L) μ d) :
    ∃ E : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
      0 ≤ E ∧
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L E = (d.genusValue : ℤ) ∧
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L E =
          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L (d.W₀ - r.S) := by
  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
      (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
  have hpos : 0 < Sheaf.h0
      ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - r.S)) := by
    rw [r.h0_one]
    norm_num
  obtain ⟨E, hE, hEc⟩ :=
    exists_effective_of_h0_pos (K := L) (d.W₀ - r.S) hpos

      (d.genusValue : ℤ) := by
    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' L, d.hdeg, r.degree]
    ring

This file closes the field-level producer left open by `Pic0SepClosedCover`.  For every field
extension `K/k` and every `mu : picEt C (overSpec k K)`, it constructs the finite separable
splitting field and all of `SepClosedTranslatedDropData`.

The positive twist stays tied to the presenting class of `mu`.  Its exponent is chosen above
both the FLV threshold and the amount needed to put the twisted class in degree at least the
genus.  The dense-point, residue-one, finite-support, and base-subtraction fields are then filled
by the rational-point-image constructor, so the output feeds the existing translated-drop
consumer without replacing `mu` by an unrelated Picard class.

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

section Producer

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]

/-- Every field-valued Picard class admits the complete lambda-tied translated-drop datum.

The nested existential is the same finite-separable splitting package used by
`exists_splitting_of_picEt`.  In particular, the returned `M₀` is certified by `hM₀` to present
the given `mu`; the positive twist, its representative, and the later base subtraction all live
in that same package. -/

    (mu : picEt C (overSpec k K)) :
    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
        (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L)
        (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L),
      Nonempty (SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) mu) := by
  obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hKL, htow, hfin, hsep, M₀, hM₀⟩ :=
    exists_splitting_of_picEt C mu
  letI := hLfield
  letI := hkL
  letI := hKL
  letI := htow
  letI := hfin
  letI := hsep
  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
      (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L

actual residual class `W₀ - S`, its base subtraction, and the presenting equation for the original

variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! A field point of `overSpec k K` is induced by its structure-field map, so degree at that
point agrees with degree at the identity.  Keeping this local avoids enlarging the base-change
API for a fact used only by the layer bridge. -/
private theorem degAt_eq_degAt_id_of_overSpec
    {K K' : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K] [Field K'] [Algebra k K']
    (lam : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (t : overSpec k K' ⟶ overSpec k K) :
    degAt lam t = degAt lam (𝟙 (overSpec k K)) := by
  let phiRing : K →+* K' := (Spec.preimage t.left).hom
  have hw : t.left ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)) =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K')) := by
    change t.left ≫ (overSpec k K).hom = (overSpec k K').hom
    exact Over.w t
  have hcat :
      CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K) ≫ Spec.preimage t.left =
        CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K') := by
    calc
      _ = Spec.preimage (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) ≫
          Spec.preimage t.left := by rw [Spec.preimage_map]
      _ = Spec.preimage
          (t.left ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))) :=
        (Spec.preimage_comp t.left
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K)))).symm
      _ = Spec.preimage (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K'))) :=
        congrArg Spec.preimage hw
      _ = _ := Spec.preimage_map _
  have hcomm : ∀ x : k,
      phiRing (algebraMap k K x) = algebraMap k K' x := by
    intro x
    exact DFunLike.congr_fun (congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom hcat) x
  let phi : K →ₐ[k] K' := AlgHom.mk phiRing hcomm
  have ht : Over.overSpecMap phi = t := by
    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
    change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom phi.toRingHom) = t.left

/-!
# Rational-point residue bridge for the translated cover

The density oracle used by the translated-cover drop has to record residue degree one at the
chosen points.  This file supplies that arithmetic bridge from the actual section certificate,
rather than adding `residueDeg = 1` as an unrelated existential field.  The relative specialization
is the exact point produced by `Over.rationalPointBaseChange`.

set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
open TopologicalSpace Opposite

/-! ## Sections have residue degree one -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_section
    {K : Type u} [Field K]
    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))}
    {e : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ X.left}
    (he : e ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
    {x : X.left}
    (hx : e.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = x) :
    X.left.residueDeg K x = 1 := by
  letI : Algebra K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra X.hom x
  have h := bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section X he hx
  have hmap :
      algebraMap K (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)) =
        X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x := by
    ext c
    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)),
      IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebraMap_eq, Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap,
      algebraMap_overStalkAlgebra]
    simp [stalkStructureHom, Scheme.overAlgebraMap]
    rfl
  letI : Algebra K (X.left.residueField x) :=
    (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x).toAlgebra
  unfold Scheme.residueDeg
  change Module.finrank K (X.left.residueField x) = 1
  apply Module.finrank_of_bijective_algebraMap
  change Function.Bijective (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x)
  rw [← hmap]
  exact h

/-! ## The base-changed rational point is such a section -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
    (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) :
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L
      ((Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L)) = 1 := by
  apply residueDeg_one_of_section
    (X := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k L)).left)
    (e := Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp)
  · exact Over.rationalPointBaseChange_snd C L p hp
  · rfl

    81	variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]

    83	  [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
    84	
    85	/-- Data for the positive twist and the subsequent point subtraction.
    86	
    87	`hM₀` ties the splitting field presentation to the particular input `mu`; `hW₀` says that the
    88	divisor being reduced is in the positive twist class (the chart index is zero at this stage).
    89	`baseSubtraction` is intentionally an explicit class-level bridge: it says that the divisor
    90	returned by the greedy reduction is represented by a base-field divisor.  The current tree has
    91	the graph-class version of this bridge but no divisor pullback operation, so this hypothesis is
    92	kept visible rather than replaced by a fieldwise existential. -/
    93	structure SepClosedTranslatedDropData (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) where
    94	  m : ℕ
    95	  M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic
    96	  hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ) =
    97	    PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀)
    98	  W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
    99	  hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
   100	    M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
   101	      (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor))
   102	  genusValue : ℕ
   103	  excess : ℕ
   104	  hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (genusValue : ℤ)
   105	  hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genusValue : ℤ) + excess
   106	  h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   107	    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)
   108	  P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
   109	  hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
   110	    (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty
   111	  hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
   112	  hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1
   113	  baseSubtraction : ∀ (S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
   114	    0 ≤ S → Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (excess : ℤ) →
   115	      (∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
   116	        coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) →
   117	      ∃ Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor,
   118	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
   119	          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
   120	            ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)
   121	
   122	/-- The output of the positive-twist/drop construction, tied to both the input class and the
   123	base-field translating divisor.
   124	
   125	The final field is the existing fibre consumer.  In particular, `S` is not merely a divisor
   126	with the right cohomology: `baseClass` identifies its class with the base change of `Z`, and
   127	`translated` is about `mu` translated by the resulting base-field class
   128	`chartTwistClass C d.m Z`. -/
   129	structure SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
   130	    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) where
   131	  S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
   132	  Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor
   133	  nonnegative : 0 ≤ S
   134	  degree : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (d.excess : ℤ)
   135	  support : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
   136	    coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ d.P
   137	  baseClass : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
   138	    Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)
   139	  h0_one : Sheaf.h0
   140	    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) = 1
   141	  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   142	    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) 1)
   143	  translated : IsSplitWitness C
   144	    (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K))
   145	
   146	/-- Positive twisting followed by point subtraction produces the exact field-level translated
   147	rank-one witness.
   148	
   149	The greedy theorem supplies `S`, `h0 = 1`, and preservation of `H1 = 0`.  The explicit
   150	`baseSubtraction` bridge then supplies the base divisor `Z`; class arithmetic shows that
   151	`W₀ - S` presents `mu` translated by the base-field class `chartTwistClass C d.m Z`.  The last
   152	line applies the existing `IsSplitWitness` consumer, so no unrelated Picard class can satisfy
   153	the conclusion. -/
   154	theorem exists_sepClosedTranslatedDropResult
   155	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
   156	    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) :
   157	    Nonempty (SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (C := C) (L := L) μ d) := by
   158	  obtain ⟨-, S, hS0, hSdeg, hSsupport, hS0one, hS1⟩ :=
   159	    exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop C μ d.m
   160	      (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   161	      d.genusValue d.excess d.hχ d.M₀ d.hM₀ d.W₀ d.hW₀ d.hdeg d.h1
   162	      d.P d.hdense d.hPcl d.hPdeg
   163	  obtain ⟨Z, hSZ⟩ := d.baseSubtraction S hS0 hSdeg hSsupport
   164	  have hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L (d.W₀ - S) =
   165	      d.M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
   166	        (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) := by
   167	    have hW₀ := d.hW₀
   168	    unfold relCurveMap relCurve at hW₀ hSZ ⊢
   169	    rw [sub_eq_add_neg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add, Scheme.picClass_neg,
   170	      hW₀, hSZ]
   171	    simp only [map_inv, inv_inv]
   172	    rw [mul_assoc, ← map_mul]
   173	    simp only [chartTwistClass, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, inv_one, mul_one,
   174	      pow_zero, one_mul]
   175	  have htranslated : IsSplitWitness C
   176	      (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K)) :=
   177	    isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ d.m Z d.M₀ d.hM₀
   178	      (d.W₀ - S) hW hS1
   179	  exact ⟨{
   180	    S := S
   181	    Z := Z
   182	    nonnegative := hS0
   183	    degree := hSdeg
   184	    support := hSsupport
   185	    baseClass := hSZ
   186	    h0_one := hS0one
   187	    h1_vanishing := hS1
   188	    translated := htranslated
   189	  }⟩
   190	
   191	end DropPackage

   193	end

     9	# The canonical native rank-one presentation contract
    10	
    11	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` deliberately leaves the geometric producer fields explicit.
    12	This file fixes the module part of that contract: for a tied cocycle datum `D`, the module is
    13	always `D.nativeModule` and its base-ring comparison is always
    14	`D.nativeModuleKSheafIso`.  The native piece trivializations supply the line-bundle field;
    15	arbitrary-cartesian pushforward base change and the cohomology/rank certificates stay as
    16	explicit obligations.
    17	
    18	The resulting contract is therefore an adapter interface for a future producer, rather than a
    19	second choice of a line bundle.  Its conversion is consumed directly by the public
    20	`PicRankOneOpen` membership theorem below; no unrelated module or untied class can enter
    21	through this bridge, and the adapter itself does not provide the geometric certificates.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    30	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    31

    33

    43	/-! ## The native adapter contract -/
    44	
    45	/--
    46	A lambda-tied rank-one presentation whose module is canonically the native module of its
    47	cocycle datum.
    48	
    49	The fields after `datum_class` are exactly the remaining producer obligations.  The line-bundle
    50	certificate is derived from the canonical piece trivializations, so a field-level H⁰/H¹
    51	calculation or an unrelated line bundle cannot be silently substituted for the native
    52	evaluation module.
    53	-/
    54	structure PicRankOneNativePresentation
    55	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
    56	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
    57	  representative : descentClasses C cover
    58	  represents :
    59	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
    60	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi

   196	theorem ne_genericPoint_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
   197	    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]

   239	/-- A divisor whose finite support consists of base-changed rational points has a Picard class

   241	
   242	The proof folds the pointwise graph-class identity over the divisor's `Finsupp` support.  It

   245	theorem exists_baseClass_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
   246	    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   247	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   248	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   249	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   250	    (S : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
   251	    (hsupp : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
   252	      (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
   253	      coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) :
   254	    ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
   255	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
   256	        Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c := by
   257	  suffices hmain : ∀ f : {x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left //
   258	      x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left} →₀ ℤ,
   259	      (∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
   260	        (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
   261	        coeffAt hx f ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) →
   262	      ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
   263	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L f =
   264	          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c from hmain S hsupp

   266	  induction f using Finsupp.induction with
   267	  | zero =>
   268	      intro _
   269	      refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
   270	      change Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L
   271	        (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor) =
   272	          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) 1
   273	      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, map_one]
   274	      rfl
   275	  | single_add p b f hpf hb ih =>
   276	      intro hsupport
   277	      have hfp : f p = 0 := Finsupp.notMem_support_iff.mp hpf
   278	      have hpMem : p.1 ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L := by
   279	        apply hsupport p.1 p.2
   280	        change (Finsupp.single p b + f) p ≠ 0
   281	        rw [Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_eq_same, hfp, add_zero]
   282	        exact hb
   283	      have hfSupport : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
   284	          (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
   285	          coeffAt hx f ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L := by
   286	        intro x hx hfx
   287	        apply hsupport x hx
   288	        change (Finsupp.single p b + f) ⟨x, hx⟩ ≠ 0
   289	        have hxp : (⟨x, hx⟩ : {z : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left //
   290	            z ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left}) ≠ p := by
   291	          intro heq
   292	          subst p
   293	          exact hfx hfp
   294	        rw [Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.single_eq_of_ne hxp, zero_add]
   295	        exact hfx
   296	      obtain ⟨cp, hcp⟩ :=
   297	        exists_baseClass_picClass_single_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
   298	          C p.1 p.2 hpMem
   299	      have key : ∀ D : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor,
   300	          (∃ cf : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
   301	            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L D =
   302	              Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) cf) →
   303	          ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
   304	            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L
   305	              (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single p.2 b + D) =
   306	              Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c := by
   307	        intro D hD
   308	        obtain ⟨cf, hcf⟩ := hD
   309	        refine ⟨cp ^ b * cf, ?_⟩
   310	        unfold relCurveMap relCurve at hcp hcf ⊢
   311	        rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add,
   312	          ← Scheme.picClass_single_zpow L p.2 b, hcp, hcf, map_mul, map_zpow]

     8	# The native module carried by a glued rank-one datum
     9	
    10	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sheaf` is already a sheaf of modules over the coefficient
    11	ring.  The presentation contract also asks for the same object as a sheaf of
    12	modules over the structure sheaf of the relative curve.  This file supplies
    13	that bridge: the componentwise `gluedQsmul` action gives a module on every open,
    14	`gluedRes_gluedQsmul` gives the semilinearity needed by
    15	`PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf`, and `gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap` identifies its
    16	restriction to the coefficient ring with the original datum sheaf.
    17	
    18	The canonical piece trivializations also prove that the native module is a line
    19	bundle.  Pushforward base-change and existence of a tied
    20	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` remain genuine producer obligations.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	
    25	universe u
    26	
    27	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    30	
    31	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    32	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    33	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    34	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
    35	
    36	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    41	
    42	/-- The structure-sheaf module on the sections of the glued datum over one open.
    43	
    44	The action is the componentwise multiplication action; the four module laws
    45	are inherited from the corresponding `gluedQsmul` identities. -/
    46	@[reducible] noncomputable def moduleOn (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) :
    47	    Module Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    48	      ((D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat)).obj (op U)) := by
    49	  change Module Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    50	    (↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit U))
    51	  letI : SMul Γ(relCurve C B, U)
    52	      (↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit U)) :=
    53	    ⟨fun r s => gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s⟩
    54	  exact Module.ofMinimalAxioms
    55	    (fun r x y => gluedQsmul_add B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r x y)
    56	    (fun r s x => gluedQsmul_add_left B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s x)
    57	    (fun r s x => gluedQsmul_mul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r s x)
    58	    (fun x => gluedQsmul_one B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U) x)
    59	
    60	/-- The presheaf of structure-sheaf modules underlying `D`. -/
    61	noncomputable def nativePresheaf : (relCurve C B).PresheafOfModules := by
    62	  let M : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat :=
    63	    D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat)
    64	  let family : ∀ U : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ,
    65	      Module ((relCurve C B).ringCatSheaf.obj.obj U) (M.obj U) :=
    66	    fun U => moduleOn D U.unop
    67	  letI : ∀ U : (relCurve C B).Opensᵒᵖ,
    68	      Module ((relCurve C B).ringCatSheaf.obj.obj U) (M.obj U) := family
    69	  exact PresheafOfModules.ofPresheaf M (by
    70	    intro X Y f r m
    71	    change gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit f.unop.le
    72	        (gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : X.unop ≤ X.unop) r m) =
    73	      gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : Y.unop ≤ Y.unop)
    74	        ((relCurve C B).resHom f.unop.le r)
    75	        (gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit f.unop.le m)
    76	    rw [gluedRes_gluedQsmul]
    77	    apply Subtype.ext
    78	    funext j
    79	    rw [gluedQsmul_coe, gluedQsmul_coe]
    80	    simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom])
    81	
    82	/-- The native `Scheme.Modules` object associated to a glued datum. -/
    83	noncomputable def nativeModule : (relCurve C B).Modules := by
    84	  refine ⟨nativePresheaf D, ?_⟩
    85	  rw [show (nativePresheaf D).presheaf =
    86	    D.sheaf.obj ⋙ (forget₂ (ModuleCat B) AddCommGrpCat) from rfl]
    87	  rw [Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    88	    (CategoryTheory.forget AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    89	  convert (Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget _ _
    90	    (CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat.{u} B))).mp D.sheaf.property using 1
    91	  all_goals rfl

    93	/-! ## Piecewise line-bundle trivializations -/
    94	
    95	/-- Sections of the native module over one cocycle piece are the structure-ring sections.
    96	
    97	The open-immersion ring equivalence transports the component trivialization from the ambient
    98	relative curve to the restricted scheme.  The `gluedTriv_gluedQsmul` identity is exactly the
    99	structure-sheaf semilinearity needed for this to be a linear equivalence over the restricted
   100	ring of sections. -/
   101	noncomputable def nativeModulePieceSectionsEquiv
   102	    (j : D.index) (V : (D.pieces j).toScheme.Opens) :
   103	    Γ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D), V) ≃ₗ[
   104	      Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V)] Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V) := by
   105	  let e := gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)
   106	  let ρ := ((D.pieces j).ι.appIso V).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   107	  let f : Γ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D), V) →ₗ[
   108	      Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V)] Γ((D.pieces j).toScheme, V) :=
   109	    { toFun := fun s => ρ (e s)
   110	      map_add' := by
   111	        intro s t
   112	        change ρ (e (s + t)) = ρ (e s) + ρ (e t)
   113	        change ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) (s + t)) =
   114	          ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s) +
   115	            ρ (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) t)
   116	        rw [show gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) (s + t) =
   117	            gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s +
   118	              gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) t by
   119	              exact (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)).map_add s t]
   120	        exact ρ.map_add _ _
   121	      map_smul' := by
   122	        intro r s
   123	        change ρ
   124	            (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)
   125	              (gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl) (ρ.symm r) s)) =
   126	          r * ρ
   127	            (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V) s)
   128	        rw [gluedTriv_gluedQsmul]
   129	        simp [ρ] }
   130	  apply LinearEquiv.ofBijective f
   131	  constructor
   132	  · intro s t h
   133	    have h' := congrArg ρ.symm h
   134	    dsimp [f] at h'
   135	    rw [ρ.symm_apply_apply, ρ.symm_apply_apply] at h'
   136	    exact (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V)).injective h'
   137	  · intro r
   138	    refine ⟨e.symm (ρ.symm r), ?_⟩
   139	    change ρ (e (e.symm (ρ.symm r))) = r
   140	    rw [e.apply_symm_apply, ρ.apply_symm_apply]
   141	
   142	/-- The piecewise section equivalences assemble to a sheaf isomorphism with the unit module. -/
   143	noncomputable def nativeModulePieceSheafIso (j : D.index) :
   144	    (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (D.pieces j).ι).obj (nativeModule D) ≅
   145	      SheafOfModules.unit (D.pieces j).toScheme.ringCatSheaf :=
   146	  (SheafOfModules.fullyFaithfulForget _).preimageIso
   147	    (PresheafOfModules.isoMk
   148	      (fun V => (nativeModulePieceSectionsEquiv D j V.unop).toModuleIso)
   149	      (fun {V W} f => by
   150	        apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
   151	        apply LinearMap.ext
   152	        intro x
   153	        change
   154	          ((D.pieces j).ι.appIso W.unop).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   155	              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le W.unop)
   156	                (gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit
   157	                  ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop)) x)) =
   158	            (D.pieces j).toScheme.presheaf.map f
   159	              (((D.pieces j).ι.appIso V.unop).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
   160	                (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x))
   161	        rw [gluedTriv_res B D.isGluingCocycle j
   162	          ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop))
   163	          ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x]
   164	        simp only [Scheme.Opens.ι_appIso]
   165	        change
   166	          (relCurve C B).resHom
   167	              ((D.pieces j).ι.image_mono (leOfHom f.unop))
   168	              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j
   169	                ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x) =
   170	            (relCurve C B).presheaf.map
   171	              ((D.pieces j).ι.opensFunctor.map f.unop).op
   172	              (gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j
   173	                ((D.pieces j).ι_image_le V.unop) x)
   174	        rfl))
   175	
   176	/-- The canonical native module is locally a free rank-one structure-sheaf module. -/
   177	theorem nativeModule_isLineBundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle (nativeModule D) := by
   178	  intro x
   179	  let j := D.pieceIndex x
   180	  refine ⟨D.pieces j, D.mem_pieces_pieceIndex x, ?_⟩
   181	  exact ⟨nativeModulePieceSheafIso D j⟩
   182	
   183	/-- On every open, restricting `D.nativeModule` to the coefficient ring recovers
   184	the datum's original module of sections.
   185	
   186	The equivalence is the identity on sections. Its linearity is the substantive
   187	point: `gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap` identifies the native structure-sheaf action
   188	of a coefficient scalar with the datum's coefficient action. -/
   189	noncomputable def nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv
   190	    (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) :
   191	    (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   192	      (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D)).obj.obj (op U) ≃ₗ[B]
   193	      D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) := by
   194	  let f :
   195	      (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   196	        (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D)).obj.obj (op U) →ₗ[B]
   197	        D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) :=
   198	    { toFun := fun x => x
   199	      map_add' := by
   200	        intros
   201	        rfl
   202	      map_smul' := by
   203	        intro r x
   204	        change gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit (le_rfl : U ≤ U)
   205	            ((relCurve C B).overAlgebraMap B U r) x =
   206	          r • (show D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U) from x)
   207	        exact gluedQsmul_overAlgebraMap B D.pieces D.unit
   208	          (le_rfl : U ≤ U) r x }
   209	  exact LinearEquiv.ofBijective f ⟨fun _ _ h => h, fun y => ⟨y, rfl⟩⟩
   210	
   211	/-- The base-ring sheaf of `D.nativeModule` is canonically the datum sheaf.
   212	
   213	This has exactly the type of `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.module_iso` when the
   214	presentation's native module is chosen to be `D.nativeModule`. -/
   215	noncomputable def nativeModuleKSheafIso :
   216	    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   217	      (Over.mk (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))) (nativeModule D) ≅ D.sheaf :=
   218	  (fullyFaithfulSheafToPresheaf _ _).preimageIso
   219	    (NatIso.ofComponents
   220	      (fun U => (nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv D U.unop).toModuleIso)
   221	      (fun {_ _} _ => by
   222	        apply ModuleCat.hom_ext
   223	        apply LinearMap.ext
   224	        intro x
   225	        rfl))
   226	
   227	end
   228

    99	the residual class `W₀ - S`.  Thus the output is directly an element of the `picDegLayer` target
   100	used by `PicRankOneOpen`, rather than a parallel existential carrier. -/

   102	    (mu : picEt C (overSpec k K))
   103	    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) mu)

   109	    have hchiC := chi_moduleKSheaf C

   111	  have hW₀ := d.hW₀
   112	  have hSZ := r.baseClass

   115	        d.M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
   116	          (chartTwistClass C d.m r.Z) := by
   117	    unfold relCurveMap relCurve at hW₀ hSZ ⊢
   118	    rw [sub_eq_add_neg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add,
   119	      Scheme.picClass_neg, hW₀, hSZ]
   120	    simp only [map_inv, inv_inv]
   121	    rw [mul_assoc, ← map_mul]
   122	    simp only [chartTwistClass, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero,

   133	      r.degree, hgenusInt]
   134	    ring

   136	  intro K' _ _ t
   137	  rw [degAt_eq_degAt_id_of_overSpec]

    13	This file closes the field-level producer left open by `Pic0SepClosedCover`.  For every field

    18	both the FLV threshold and the amount needed to put the twisted class in degree at least the
    19	genus.  The dense-point, residue-one, finite-support, and base-subtraction fields are then filled
    20	by the rational-point-image constructor, so the output feeds the existing translated-drop
    21	consumer without replacing `mu` by an unrelated Picard class.

    68	  letI := htow

    85	  haveI : IsProper (baseChangeBundle C L).hom :=
    86	    instIsProperSndLeft C L

    90	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
    91	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
    92	      ((baseChangeBundle C L).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    93	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
    94	  haveI : QuasiCompact
    95	      ((baseChangeBundle C L).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    96	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L

    99	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L

   122	    simp [m]

   138	        (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)))

   140	      Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L)).left)

   142	            (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)) =
   143	        thetaL ^ m := by
   144	    simp only [thetaL, chartTwistClass, Over.tensorObj_left, overSpec_left,
   145	      Over.coe_hom, Algebra.algebraMap_self, CommRingCat.ofHom_id,

    18	
    19	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
    20	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
    21	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
    22	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
    23	
    24	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
    25	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
    26	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
    27	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;

    31	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.

     9	/-!
    10	# The presentation locus for the rank-one Abel map
    11	
    12	`PicRankOneOpen` is the functorial locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer whose pullback to
    13	every affine test admits a tied `PicRankOneLocalPresentation`.  Quantifying after every affine
    14	pullback makes the condition intrinsic on arbitrary test schemes; stability under further
    15	pullback is exactly `picEtMap_comp`.
    16	
    17	The remaining declarations form the corresponding preimages in the widened divisor functor and
    18	in its canonical representing Yoneda functor, together with the restricted Abel transformations.
    19	These are logical subfunctors only.  In particular, this file does not assert that
    20	`PicRankOneOpen` is represented by an open subscheme.  The relative-openness acceptance gate and
    21	the conditional universal-divisor carrier contract are exposed separately in `DivRankOneOpen.lean`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    26	
    27	universe u
    28	
    29	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    30	
    31	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    32	
    33	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    34	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    35	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    36	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    37	
    38	noncomputable section
    39	
    40	/-- The rank-one presentation locus in the degree-`genus C` Picard layer.
    41	
    42	Membership means that every affine pullback of the input plus class admits a local presentation
    43	tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
    44	locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
    45	def PicRankOneOpen :
    46	    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
    47	  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    48	      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    49	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    50	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}
    51	  map {T T'} f lam hlam A _ _ t := by
    52	    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)
    53	    have e : F.map t.op (F.map f lam) = F.map (t ≫ f.unop).op lam := by
    54	      apply Subtype.ext
    55	      exact (picEtMap_comp C f.unop t lam.1).symm
    56	    rw [e]
    57	    exact hlam A (t ≫ f.unop)
    58	
    59	/-! ## The public membership contract -/
    60	
    61	/-- The exact producer predicate for the rank-one locus.
    62	
    63	This is intentionally lambda-tied and quantifies over every affine pullback.  In particular, it
    64	is stronger than a field-fibre `h⁰ = 1`/`H¹ = 0` statement: a producer must supply the complete
    65	`PicRankOneLocalPresentation` structure for the pulled-back class. -/
    66	def PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition
    67	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    68	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) : Prop :=
    69	  ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    70	    (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    71	    Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    72	      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))
    73	
    74	/-- Unfolded membership in `PicRankOneOpen`, with the presentation tied to the pulled-back
    75	Picard class.  Keeping this predicate named is important for producers in later lanes: a
    76	field-level divisor or chart witness is not a substitute for this arbitrary-affine-pullback
    77	contract. -/
    78	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_iff {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    79	    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) :
    80	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔
    81	      ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    82	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    83	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    84	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam)) := by
    85	  rfl
    86	
    87	/-- Constructor for the exact lambda-tied arbitrary-affine-pullback presentation contract. -/
    88	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations
    89	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    90	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    91	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    92	        (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),
    93	        Nonempty (PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi
    94	          ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))) :
    95	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
    96	  (mem_picRankOneOpen_iff pi lam).mpr h
    97	
    98	/-- Constructor using the named arbitrary-affine producer predicate. -/
    99	theorem mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentationCondition
   100	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   101	    {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   102	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.LocalPresentationCondition pi lam) :
   103	    lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T := by
   104	  exact mem_picRankOneOpen_of_localPresentations pi h
   105	
   106	/-- The inclusion of the public rank-one locus into its degree-genus ambient functor. -/
   107	def picRankOneOpenIncl :
   108	    (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ) :=
   109	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   110	
   111	/-- The same inclusion after the slice-to-big-site `Σ` extension.
   112	
   113	`IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` is a property of presheaves on schemes.  The rank-one functor is
   114	defined on the slice over `Spec k`, so the `Σ` extension is the category-correct carrier for the
   115	relative-open gate below. -/
   116	def picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl :
   117	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor ⟶
   118	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
   119	  Over.sigmaExtensionNat (PicRankOneOpen pi).ι
   120	
   121	/-- Relative openness of the public locus, in Mathlib's presheaf sense.
   122	
   123	This is a named acceptance gate rather than an unproved global assertion.  A future geometric
   124	producer discharges it by supplying the represented open pullbacks; no arbitrary `Subfunctor` is
   125	silently treated as an open subscheme. -/
   126	def PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen : Prop :=
   127	  IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi)
   128	
   129	/-! ## The explicit fibre producer contract -/
   130	
   131	/-- A fibre of the rank-one locus over one test class, presented by an open of that test.
   132	
   133	The `exists_factor` field is tied to the displayed class `g` and to an arbitrary source value `v`.
   134	It is the family-level content needed for relative representability; the open immersion itself
   135	supplies uniqueness of the factor.  Thus this structure cannot be inhabited by an unrelated open
   136	or by a fieldwise dimension statement. -/
   137	structure PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   138	    {X : Scheme.{u}}
   139	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   140	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))) where
   141	  W : X.Opens
   142	  fst : yoneda.obj (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶
   143	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor
   144	  sq : fst ≫ picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi = yoneda.map W.ι ≫ g
   145	  exists_factor : ∀ (S : Scheme.{u})
   146	    (v : (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor).obj (Opposite.op S))
   147	    (w : S ⟶ X),
   148	    (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (Opposite.op S) v =
   149	      g.app (Opposite.op S) w →
   150	    ∃ u : S ⟶ (W : Scheme.{u}),
   151	      fst.app (Opposite.op S) u = v ∧ u ≫ W.ι = w
   152	
   153	namespace PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   154	
   155	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
   156	variable {g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   157	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))}
   158	
   159	/-- The fibre square supplied by `FibrePresented` is a pullback of presheaves. -/
   160	theorem isPullback (D : PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g) :
   161	    IsPullback D.fst (yoneda.map D.W.ι) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g := by
   162	  refine IsPullback.of_forall_isPullback_app fun S => ?_
   163	  rw [Types.isPullback_iff]
   164	  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   165	  · exact congrArg (fun φ : yoneda.obj (D.W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶
   166	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) =>
   167	      φ.app S) D.sq
   168	  · rintro u₁ u₂ ⟨-, h₂⟩
   169	    exact (cancel_mono D.W.ι).mp h₂
   170	  · intro v w hvw
   171	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := D.exists_factor S.unop v w hvw
   172	    exact ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩
   173	
   174	end PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented
   175	
   176	/-- An arbitrary-test fibre producer discharges the relative openness gate. -/
   177	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_fibrePresented
   178	    (D : ∀ (X : Scheme.{u})
   179	      (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   180	        Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))),
   181	      PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented pi g) :
   182	    PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi := by
   183	  refine MorphismProperty.relative.of_exists ?_
   184	  intro X g
   185	  let d := D X g
   186	  exact ⟨d.W, d.fst, d.W.ι, d.isPullback, inferInstance⟩
   187	
   188	/-- Expose a supplied relative-open certificate without hiding it behind typeclass search. -/
   189	theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_certificate
   190	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi :=
   191	  h
   192	
   193	/-- Extract the open immersion supplied by the relative-openness certificate on an arbitrary
   194	pullback.  This is the exact shape consumed by an eventual chart/fibre producer. -/
   195	theorem picRankOneOpen_openPullback
   196	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi)
   197	    {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
   198	    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
   199	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)))
   200	    (fst : yoneda.obj Z ⟶
   201	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor)
   202	    (snd : Z ⟶ X)
   203	    (hpb : IsPullback fst (yoneda.map snd) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g) :
   204	    IsOpenImmersion snd :=
   205	  h.property g fst snd hpb

   207	/-- Pullback stability of the public rank-one locus, exposed independently of its definition. -/
   208	theorem picRankOneOpen_map_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   209	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   210	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   211	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   212	  (PicRankOneOpen pi).map f h
   213	
   214	/-- Pullback stability of the public locus, with the base-change direction made explicit. -/
   215	theorem picRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   216	    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
   217	    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
   218	    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
   219	  picRankOneOpen_map_mem pi f h

   224	open subscheme `DivRankOneOpen`. -/

    10	# `IsChartDatumPresentation`: the FORWARD half, from a pointwise plus-class identity
    11	
    12	`IsChartDatumPresentation μ D` (`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean:161`) is CHART-U(b)'s one
    13	remaining residue: an `↔`, at every point `t` of an affine test, between
    14	
    15	* `D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing κ(t)` — the datum's fibre predicate, and
    16	* `IsSplitWitness C (fibre of μ at κ(t))` — the split predicate `chartLocus` is defined by.
    17	
    18	That file's header prices it as a *construction* rather than bookkeeping, and is right to: the
    19	splitting field `L` in `IsSplitWitness` is quantified **per point**, so no single datum obviously
    20	matches it everywhere.
    21	
    22	**This file discharges the `→` direction from a hypothesis that mentions no witness at all.**
    23	
    24	## What makes the forward direction cheap now
    25	
    26	The datum side hands you a witness divisor `W` over `κ(t)` in the class
    27	`CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A κ(t)) D.cechPicClass`, with vanishing `H¹`.  To build
    28	`IsSplitWitness` you must exhibit a finite separable extension over which the *fibre of `μ`* is
    29	honest, with a witness in its class.  Take the extension to be `κ(t)` itself — the identity
    30	extension, finite and separable — and the witness to be `W`.
    31	
    32	That is exactly `isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness_self`
    33	(`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean`), the trivial splitting `L := K`.  Memory item I-0564 had
    34	recorded that instance as **unelaborable** and singled it out as "worth wanting"; it is a
    35	one-liner once the existentials are staged rather than bundled, and this file is the first
    36	consumer that needed it.
    37	
    38	So the whole forward direction reduces to a statement with **no witness, no `H¹`, no divisor**:
    39	that the datum's fibre class, read as a plus class, *is* the fibre of `μ`.  That is
    40	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre` below — a naturality identity between `PicEtAff.map ∘ picEtAffineEquiv`
    41	and `relPicMk ∘ CechPic.map`, one equation per point.
    42

    44	
    45	The `←` direction.  It is the genuinely harder one and it is where the per-point quantification
    46	of `L` bites: from `IsSplitWitness` you receive *some* extension `L_t/κ(t)`, varying with `t`,
    47	and must produce the datum's predicate at `κ(t)` itself — i.e. descend the witness along
